title: Bo: this month is yours (Exodus 12:1–2)
hookLine: the first command to the whole people is to mark time by the new moon

cards: Look at a work schedule someone else wrote for you. Shifts, breaks, the hour you may leave. Now imagine that for your whole life, and your parents' lives, every hour belonged to someone else.
That's slavery's calendar: the master owns the clock. The plagues are almost over. One more, the worst, is coming.

And right here, before anyone has left Egypt, God gives Moses and Aaron the first command meant for the whole people. You might expect something about freedom, or worship, or the law. It's about the moon.

teach.h: THIS MONTH SHALL BE UNTO YOU.
teach.b: Here's the verse, in the old Jewish translation: "This month shall be unto you the beginning of months; it shall be the first month of the year to you."
The Hebrew for month is chodesh, and Jewish tradition hears in it chadash, new. A month is a new moon, a renewal.
Tradition draws the Jewish calendar from this verse: months by the moon, kept in step with the sun so the spring festival stays in spring.
In ancient times a court in Jerusalem declared the new month, after witnesses came to say they'd seen the thin new crescent.
Tradition says the calendar was later fixed by calculation, which is how it runs today. And the first day of each month, Rosh Chodesh, is still marked with extra prayers.

Rashi, the medieval commentator, opens his whole Torah commentary with a question about this verse. Why didn't the Torah simply begin here, with the first command given to Israel? He has his own answer, about the land.
But the question shows how weighty this verse was to him.
Sforno, a later Italian commentator, noticed the small word unto you. Until now, he says, their days belonged to others. From here on, the months are theirs.
Before a free people can do anything else, it has to own its time.

how: Jews mark Rosh Chodesh, the new month, with added prayers including Hallel, and in synagogue the coming new month is announced on the Shabbat before. Some people also say a blessing over the waxing moon each month, Kiddush Levanah.

games.q: the plagues are almost over. no one has left Egypt yet. what's the first command God gives the whole people?
o: mark your months by the new moon.
games.why: this month shall be unto you the beginning of months. a people still enslaved is first handed its own calendar.

practice: Say today's date to yourself, the day of the week, the month, the year, not as a deadline but as a fact you choose to notice, and if you know the Hebrew date, say that too.
Then ask which hours today are yours to shape, maybe only ten minutes on a bus, and decide now what one stretch is for. If you pray, you can offer that stretch of time.

wordCard.voice: Bo. Our portion still. Today, its first command to a people not yet free: count your months by the new moon. Time becomes theirs.

orig.note: Hebrew: month, or new moon; the same root as chadash, new.

carryVoice: Your line: own your time. The moon keeps the count, and the months are yours. That's day three hundred thirty-five.
